incidents.summary: The Place Search translations public low alarm was triggered by elevated 4xx responses associated with the API key "los-MobileApp-ChargingTariffsCompositeService"; the correlated API Gateway alarm recovered and remained stable. Historical recurrence shows similar translations-endpoint failures, including 400 and 429 responses from this caller and a more recent occurrence involving the "pcmcs-charging" API key.

resolutionSuggestions.investigation: Inspect Place Search/API Gateway request logs for the translations endpoint during the alert window, grouped by API key and HTTP status, with priority on "los-MobileApp-ChargingTariffsCompositeService"; confirm whether the recovered 4xx burst was predominantly invalid requests (400-class) or quota/throttling responses (429). Sources: INC000111017340, INC000111194980, INC000110880719.
resolutionSuggestions.mitigation: Engage the owner of "los-MobileApp-ChargingTariffsCompositeService" with request examples and status-code breakdown, then correct malformed translations requests and/or apply client-side request shaping appropriate to the observed failure type. Historical records explicitly identify this key and previously observed 400/429 responses for /translations. Sources: INC000111017340, INC000111194980, INC000110880719.
resolutionSuggestions.resolutionNote: Validated that the translations-endpoint 4xx alarm was associated with API key "los-MobileApp-ChargingTariffsCompositeService"; reviewed the status-code/request pattern with the caller owner, applied or agreed corrective action as applicable, and confirmed the alarm recovered and remained stable. Sources: INC000111017340, INC000111194980, INC000110880719.

resolutionSuggestions.investigation: Check whether 429 responses contributed to the alert and compare request rate, concurrency, retry behavior, and request fan-out for the affected API key against the period before recovery. Sources: INC000110880719, INC000110767041.
resolutionSuggestions.mitigation: If throttling is confirmed, have the consuming client reduce burstiness through bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter, concurrency limits, and avoidance of duplicate translations calls; validate any quota or backend-capacity change separately before applying it. Sources: INC000110880719, INC000110767041.
resolutionSuggestions.resolutionNote: Analysis found that translations requests from the affected client included throttling-related responses; client request pacing/retry behavior was reviewed and corrective action was applied or tracked with the consuming team. The CloudWatch alarm subsequently recovered and remained stable. Sources: INC000110880719, INC000110767041.

resolutionSuggestions.investigation: Extend the review beyond the initially identified key to determine whether other consumers contributed to the translations 4xx metric, specifically checking for "pcmcs-charging" and correlating the metric with the parent API Gateway 4xx alarm. Sources: INC000111017340, INC000111230726.
resolutionSuggestions.mitigation: Maintain per-API-key and per-status-code triage for translations alarms so a caller-specific 4xx burst can be routed to the responsible consumer quickly; use the Place Search collaboration process for cross-team prioritization when a caller-side fix requires coordination. Sources: INC000111017340, INC000111230726.
resolutionSuggestions.resolutionNote: Correlated the translations 4xx metric with API Gateway errors and reviewed contributing API keys, including the affected caller(s). The responsible consumer team was engaged where needed, and the alarm recovered with no continuing elevated error rate. Sources: INC000111017340, INC000111230726.

incidents.summary: Customer’s ID7/HU_MGU navigation shows German gas stations without prices when searching along the route near 49.20378, 8.59601 on 2026-08-29, while fuel prices display normally for France and Spain, indicating a Germany-specific fuel price data or entitlement issue rather than connectivity or hardware.

resolutionSuggestions.suggestion: Verify the DE fuel price provider/feed status (EMEA PROD) around 2026-08-29 13:34 UTC; check backend health dashboards and logs for Germany-only fuel price services (e.g., TPEG/POI price feed) to confirm a regional data outage or suppression.

Re-provision ConnectedDrive entitlements for fuel price display (Germany) for the VIN and push a service refresh to the head unit; after backend refresh, ask the customer to toggle Data Privacy/Online Services off/on to force token renewal and data reload.

Confirm that any market-specific legal/consent requirements for displaying fuel prices in Germany are accepted; if applicable, re-prompt the customer to accept fuel price terms and conditions in the HMI or via their ConnectedDrive account and then retry.

Check HMI filters and fuel type selection: clear all filters (show all fuels), test both the Thematic Map ‘Gas stations’ and the POI list via Online Search (at location vs along route); if list view shows prices but the thematic overlay doesn’t, log a UI/overlay defect for ID7.

Ensure the head unit is on the latest available software and online map components; if there is a known defect affecting German fuel prices on iStep 23-11-550, plan an update to the corrective iStep or deploy the relevant online component fix, then retest.

If a backend/provider issue is confirmed, communicate outage scope and ETA to the customer and offer a temporary workaround (e.g., using the BMW app or an external app to view DE fuel prices) until the feed is restored.
